outlook: Wheat led grains lower Wednesday as progress toward U.S.-Ukraine-Russia peace talks, expected in Abu Dhabi in November, eased Black Sea supply worries: Chicago December wheat fell 11¼ cents to $5.99 and Minneapolis December spring wheat lost 7½ cents to $6.21, despite IKAR cutting its Russian wheat export forecast to 29 million tonnes. December corn gained 3 cents to $4.51¾ on slow harvest progress (60% done vs. 66% average, with rain expected), while November soybeans slipped 4¾ cents to $12.24½ as a weaker Brazilian real makes Brazilian beans more competitive. ICE November canola eased C$2.00 to C$773.70 alongside lower soybean oil. Cash bids shown are from Tuesday's USDA Minneapolis report; Wednesday's report was not yet posted.
